topStory.headline: Middlesex College Students Selected for New Jersey A.I. Government Fellowship
topStory.summary:
Two Middlesex College computer science students, Laila Diaz and Hassan Ibrahim, have been selected from over 250 applicants for New Jersey's A.I. for Impact Community College Fellowship, according to Insider NJ. The semester-long program pairs students with the State Office of Innovation, where they work 20 hours per week on government A.I. projects while receiving stipends and continuing their studies.

Ibrahim is working on machine learning models for I.T. ticketing systems, while Diaz is creating an A.I. Slack bot for engineers. These projects address operational challenges in government settings. Ibrahim stated his interest in working with A.I. "in an ethical way" and understanding how the technology functions "in a regulated, government setting." Diaz expressed interest in cybersecurity work for government, describing it as "working for my community."

The New Jersey Council of County Colleges administers the program, with funding from the Economic Development Authority and hosting by the State Office of Innovation. The partnership model recognizes community colleges as participants in A.I. workforce development alongside four-year institutions.

stories.headline: Higher Ed IT Leaders Focus on A.I. Risk Management Frameworks
stories.summary: EdTech Magazine explores how continuous threat exposure management can help universities handle A.I.-related risks. The approach emphasizes understanding what A.I. systems exist on campus, prioritizing which matter most, and creating frameworks for ongoing risk reduction as new tools emerge.

stories.headline: State and Local Governments Deploy A.I. for Public Services
stories.summary: State and local governments are deploying A.I. for operations from public defender case review to real-time meeting translation, according to GovTech. Michigan's Allegan County reports an 8-9% increase in case clearance after implementing A.I. video analysis tools, while North Las Vegas provides live translation in virtually any language for public meetings.
